summary: EARTHBEAT is an interactive Earth-science data sonification platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, The Earth Information Jukebox. It transforms Earth data into sound, allowing users to explore our planet through an engaging audio experience. Users can discover different Earth phenomena, listen to data-inspired soundscapes, and understand how scientific information can be experienced beyond traditional charts and visualizations. EARTHBEAT aims to make Earth science more accessible, interactive, and engaging.
details:
EARTHBEAT is an interactive web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, under the challenge "The Earth Information Jukebox."

The project transforms Earth science information into sound, allowing users to explore our planet through interactive audio experiences. Instead of only viewing scientific information through charts and images, users can listen to soundscapes inspired by different Earth phenomena.

The application includes several experiences:

  • Ocean Symphony
  • Night Frequencies
  • Lightning Pulse
  • Atmospheric Waves
  • Carbon Soundscape
  • Forest Frequencies
  • Atmospheric River

Users can explore these experiences through an interactive website and listen to the corresponding soundscapes.

Our goal is to make Earth science more engaging, accessible, and easier to explore through data sonification. The project combines Earth science, sound, and interactive web technology to create a different way of experiencing information about our planet.

We developed the application using Antigravity IDE and used GitHub for source code management and Vercel for deployment. The project uses web development technologies, interactive components, and audio features to deliver the experience.

Project website: https://earthbeat.vercel.app
Source code: https://github.com/vedantIShereTOcook/earthbeat
